title: Tissue Engineering of Tumor Stromal Microenvironment with Application to Cancer Cell Invasion
protocol: Dissolve 29 mg of L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate per 5 ml of DMEM solution.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm membrane filter.
Store as 0.25 ml sterile aliquots in -20 °C.
Add 0.25 ml aliquot of 200x L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate stock to every 50 ml of fibroblast media on the day required.
Prepare keratinocyte growth media as follows:
Mix 300 ml of DMEM and 100 ml of Ham’s F-12 supplemented with 10% FBS.
Add 0.4 mg/ml hydrocortisone to the mixture.
Add 5 mg/ml insulin to the mixture.
Add 10 ng/ml EGF to the mixture.
Add 5 mg/ml transferrin to the mixture.
Add 8.4 ng/ml cholera toxin to the mixture.
Add 13 ng/ml liothyronine to the mixture.
Add 1x penicillin-streptomycin solution to the mixture.
Seed 200,000 fibroblasts per well in 6-well plates at a density of 20,000 cells/cm² in fibroblast media supplemented with L-ascorbic acid 2-phosphate.
Refeed the wells every 2-3 days with 2-5 ml of fresh media as needed.
Gently scrape the circumference of the matrix layer with a 1 ml micropipette tip after six weeks to release it from the plate.
Push the edges of the released matrix towards the center of the well to detach it easily and allow it to float in the media.
Spread out the floating native matrix in the media to prevent folding.
Change the media every 2-3 days during the 5-day remodeling period.
Transfer the remodeled, thicker native matrix gently onto a Nylon net using blunt forceps.
Spread the matrix layer flat on the Nylon net using a 1 ml micropipette tip and blunt forceps.
Prepare sterile clonal cylinders by smearing a small amount of sterile Vaseline on one end.
Place clonal cylinders on the native matrix with the Vaseline side down.
Add cSCC cells (250,000 cells in 100 µl of keratinocyte growth media) to the clonal cylinders.
Remove the clonal cylinders after 6 hours when the cSCC cells have settled.
Lift the Nylon net with the native matrix and cSCC cells to an air-liquid interface onto bent stainless steel wire mesh support.
Add keratinocyte growth media supplemented with ascorbic acid until the media level touches the bottom of the native matrix.
Change the media every 2-3 days.
Harvest at 7 and 14 days post-seeding of cSCC cells.
Fix harvested samples in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight at room temperature.
Bisect the fixed samples and embed them in wax for formalin-fixed paraffin embedded blocks with the cut surface facing outwards.
Alternatively, bisected samples can be embedded in OCT and snap-frozen immediately in liquid nitrogen for fresh frozen tissue blocks.
Cut 4 μm sections on a microtome.
Dewax the sections if necessary.
Stain the sections using standard haematoxylin and eosin.
Perform immunohistology staining to visualize cSCC cells using mouse monoclonal antibody against keratin 14 (LL001, in-house).
